discovery_method: One of the 12 verifiable production candidates in output/xstream-1.4.17-to-1.4.19-forbiddenclass_candidates.jsonl (repo einsteinarbert/axon-saga-example, sha dddd794b).

library.dependency_scope: compile (transitive via org.axonframework axon-spring-boot-starter 4.6.1; resolves xstream 1.4.19)

in_repo_version_transition.mechanism: transitive via an Axon bump (no direct xstream bump)
in_repo_version_transition.evidence: order-service/pom.xml (the module holding the adaptation) went axon-spring-boot-starter 4.0.3 -> 4.6.1. Axon 4.0.3 resolves xstream 1.4.10; Axon 4.6.1 resolves xstream 1.4.19. So the transitive xstream crossed the 1.4.18 boundary within the repo's own history.
in_repo_version_transition.corrected_2026_08_04: This block previously read crossed_boundary: false with 'axon-spring-boot-starter 4.6.1 was set in the first commit 0fbef3c and never bumped'. That inspected the ROOT pom; the adaptation lives in order-service/, whose module pom had 4.0.3 at the first commit (0fbef3c5, 2019-04-14) and was bumped to 4.6.1 at fad9b942 (2022-10-25). Found by resolve_version.py, which resolves the version the build actually gets rather than the declared one.

bump_provenance.summary: There is NO commit in this repo that bumps xstream. The boundary-crossing xstream version was never chosen or upgraded by the developer — it arrived transitively through the Axon starter, which was pinned once in the very first commit.
bump_provenance.how_introduced_transitively: The app never declares com.thoughtworks.xstream:xstream directly. It depends on org.axonframework:axon-spring-boot-starter 4.6.1, and Axon uses XStream as its default event/command serializer, so the starter pulls xstream in transitively. Maven resolves that transitive dependency to xstream 1.4.19 (already past the 1.4.18 default-deny boundary). So from the first build the app runs on a post-1.4.18 xstream without any explicit version being written anywhere.
evidence: `git log -S 'xstream' -- '**/pom.xml'` over the full history returns NOTHING — the xstream version string never appears in any committed pom.

No pom declares a com.thoughtworks.xstream dependency (the only such line, order-service/pom.xml, is the explicit dep ADDED by the verification harness to pin the version for the differential — not an app commit).
axon 4.6.1 is set in the very first commit 0fbef3c ('First Commit') and never bumped afterward — so the transitive xstream version is fixed from project creation.
The adaptation commit dddd794b touches the poms only to REMOVE Swagger 3.0.0 dependencies; it does not change the xstream or axon version at all.
bump_provenance.why_it_still_breaks: Because the resolved xstream (1.4.19) is already on the default-deny side of the 1.4.18 boundary, the break is present at runtime the moment the app serializes its own command/event type through Axon's XStream — no upgrade event is needed to trigger it. The developer discovered it as a runtime ForbiddenClassException and responded with the adaptation commit (see `adaptation.commit`), which is the only xstream-related change in the repo.
bump_provenance.consequence_for_the_dataset: The 'library version transition' is implicit in the dependency tree rather than materialized as a diff. The 3-state differential recreates the transition synthetically (pinning xstream 1.4.17 -> 1.4.19 via the harness dep) to isolate the version + the adaptation as the only variables.

adaptation.repo_note: A saga-pattern Axon/Spring-Boot sample (Spring Boot 2.7.5, Axon 4.6.1, Java 11). Multi-module Maven; 'core-apis' holds the shared command/event domain types, 'order-service' holds the XStream config.
adaptation.xstreamconfig_was_new: XStreamAutoConfiguration was CREATED in this commit (a Spring @Configuration producing an XStream @Bean plus a nested config whose @PostConstruct registers converters and applies the allowlist). At the parent the app relied on Axon's default plain XStream.
adaptation.in_repo_causal_evidence: Commit message and the added class name the exact exception (ForbiddenClassException); the fix is the allowlist on the app's domain package.
adaptation.summary: Added a production XStreamAutoConfiguration that allowlists the app's com.progressivecoder.ecommerce.** domain package on the XStream Axon uses, satisfying xstream 1.4.18 default-deny.

behavioral_break.mechanism: xstream 1.4.18+ default-deny: fromXML on a non-allowlisted class throws com.thoughtworks.xstream.security.ForbiddenClassException. Axon uses XStream as its default serializer, so a plain XStream (no allowlist) rejects the app's own command/event types under >=1.4.18.

verification.method: 3-state differential at the adapted commit (Maven, JDK 11). The configured state drives the REAL production code path: XStreamAutoConfiguration.xStream(Optional.empty()) then XStreamConverterAutoConfiguration.registerConverters(), contrasted against a plain new XStream() (faithful stand-in for Axon's pre-adaptation default), swapping only the xstream version.
verification.test: bbc.XstreamBbcTest (authored JUnit5; round-trip a CreateOrderCommand through XStream, assert orderId survives). Preserved in scratchpad/xstream-axon-saga-einsteinarbert-harness/.
verification.harness_notes: order-service/pom.xml edited to add an EXPLICIT depth-1 xstream dependency version=${bbc.xstream.version} so the baseline override applies (otherwise xstream is pinned to 1.4.19 transitively by Axon). Test written for JUnit5 (jupiter already on the classpath via Spring Boot 2.7.5); a JUnit4 test was not discovered because surefire runs on the JUnit Platform without the vintage engine.
verification.conclusion: Confirmed BBC with a real external native-Maven production adaptation: baseline passes, the same plain-XStream code breaks only under xstream >=1.4.18 with a ForbiddenClassException on the app's own command type, and the production XStreamAutoConfiguration allowlist resolves it.
